findings: Material concurrency gap: TDD.md's coaching body carries revisionId, idempotencyKey and optional supersedesRequestId, but no caller-observed progress version. Admission chooses successfulStages + 1 and only rejects an active request. Two distinct keys issued from the same workspace state can overlap, yet if B's admission is delayed until A has committed and cleared the active pointer, B remains on the same revision and is admitted for the next stage. This can consume two stages and application stage charges for overlapping actions, contrary to COACH-06. The active-request lock protects simultaneous active work but does not fence a stale action after fast completion. Add and fingerprint an expected progression/version, check it for new admissions, and explicitly test the delayed-admission ordering.

limitations: This planning pass read only planning-task.md, planning-owner-requirements.json, and PRD.md, TDD.md and RequirementsToTests.md in sample-08 and sample-31. It did not inspect other artifacts, raw owner transcripts, histories, telemetry, method labels or external resources, and did not change delivery judgments.

These are draft plans, not application implementations. Planned tests and concurrency protocols were reviewed statically; no feature tests, database migrations, compiler checks or provider calls were executed or independently verified.

Owner-confirmed constraints are judged against the supplied COACH-01 through COACH-15 answers. Proposed interfaces, recovery mechanics and educational stage wording are not treated as additional owner-confirmed facts. Claims about how owner answers were retrieved were not independently verified from raw transcripts.

The real product repository/schema was not inspected. Feasibility is assessed against the supplied Node24, React/MUI, Express, Better Auth database-session, PostgreSQL/Prisma, shared Zod and offline AiProvider baseline; exact integration compatibility remains to be reviewed during implementation.

Both samples explicitly leave retention/deletion and live-provider numeric/capability verification as pre-real-user or production gates. These truthfully pending owner decisions are allowed and are not scored as missing scope or approvals. Both deny human approval and executed-feature-test claims.
